claims.claim: Total revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $17.2 billion.
Second-quarter revenue represented a one percent year-over-year increase.
GAAP diluted earnings per share from continuing operations were $2.27 in the second quarter.
GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations was down two percent versus the prior-year period.
Operating (non-GAAP) diluted earnings per share for the quarter were $2.93.
Operating (non-GAAP) diluted EPS increased five percent year-over-year.
The company reported a gross profit margin of 57.7 percent on a GAAP basis.
The company reported a gross profit margin of 59.4 percent on an operating (non-GAAP) basis.
Net income from continuing operations was $2.2 billion for the quarter.
Pre-tax income from continuing operations was $2.5 billion for the quarter.
The pre-tax income margin from continuing operations was 14.4 percent.
For the first six months of 2026, total revenue reached $33.1 billion.
Six-month revenue was up five percent year-over-year.
GAAP diluted earnings per share for the year-to-date period were $3.55.
Software revenue grew five percent to $7.8 billion.
Data revenues increased 19 percent, contributing to Software growth.
Hybrid Cloud (Red Hat) revenues rose 11 percent, contributing to Software growth.
Transaction Processing revenues declined eight percent.
Consulting revenues were flat at $5.3 billion.
Strategy and Technology and Intelligent Operations were both flat as reported and both grew one percent at constant currency.
Infrastructure revenues decreased seven percent to $3.8 billion.
IBM Z revenues fell 42 percent.
Distributed Infrastructure revenues rose 37 percent.
Distributed Infrastructure built an order backlog of nearly $500 million.
The company now expects full-year constant currency revenue growth in the range of four-to-five percent.
At current foreign exchange rates, currency is expected to be neutral to growth for the year.
IBM continues to expect full-year 2026 free cash flow to increase by about $1 billion year-over-year.
Management expects improved pre-tax income margin expansion for the full year.
The expected margin expansion is attributed to productivity efforts and AI-driven operational efficiencies.
The company generated net cash from operating activities of $2.6 billion in the second quarter, up $0.9 billion year-over-year.
Second-quarter free cash flow was $2.5 billion, down $0.3 billion year-over-year.
IBM ended the second quarter with $8.2 billion in cash, restricted cash and marketable securities, a decrease of $6.3 billion from year-end 2025.
Total debt, including IBM Financing debt of $13.0 billion, totaled $62.0 billion, up $0.7 billion year-to-date.
The company invested $10.5 billion in acquisitions during the first six months of the year.
Software results diverged, with Data and Hybrid Cloud growing while Transaction Processing declined eight percent.
Infrastructure results show IBM Z down 42 percent partly offset by Distributed Infrastructure up 37 percent.
The company reported $10.5 billion in acquisitions for the first half of the year while debt increased.
